chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about two men, each one of the two fabricated upon his companion. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Penalty (Hadd) would be staved off from them, and they would both be reprimanded'.

key_terms.يُعَزَّرَانِ: They are both subjected to discretionary reprimand

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when two people fabricate against each other?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that when two parties mutually accuse each other of a crime (tafari), the strict fixed penalty (Hadd) is suspended to avoid the risk of error, and they are instead subjected to Ta'zir (discretionary punishment). This reflects the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing caution (ihtiyat) in applying Hadd penalties, ensuring that the severity of the fixed punishment is not applied unless the evidence is irrefutable. The decision to defer Hadd underscores the importance of judicial discretion in maintaining justice when mutual culpability creates ambiguity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunush, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
